title: By faith (Hebrews 11:1–16)
hookLine: faith is the substance of things hoped for; Abraham went out not knowing
carry: the evidence of things not seen
tomorrow: who gets left off the list when the well-known names run out?

lines: HOW DO YOU PACK FOR THAT?
cards: A suitcase lies open on the bed, and the one fact you'd need to fill it is missing. Beach or snow? A week or a year?

Hebrews says Abraham packed like that: "By faith Abraham, when he was called to go out into a place which he should after receive for an inheritance, obeyed; and he went out, not knowing whither he went."
Not knowing whither: no address, no map. So how do you pack for that? Hebrews eleven answers with one sentence, and the rest of the chapter leans on it.

teach.b: Here's the sentence: "Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen." Substance is something solid, ground you can stand on. Evidence is what convinces you.
And you already live by evidence of things not seen.
Keys in the front door, a bag dropped in the hall, a particular cough: you know who's home before you see them. That's the picture here. Faith isn't a blind guess.
It's hearing the keys and getting up to say hello. So how does Abraham pack? Light.
He lived in tents, a stranger in the very land he'd been promised.

Then the chapter says something it doesn't soften: "These all died in faith, not having received the promises, but having seen them afar off." They never arrived. They saw it in the distance and greeted it anyway.

teach.h: THE EVIDENCE OF THINGS NOT SEEN.
teach.b: They "confessed that they were strangers and pilgrims on the earth," and looked for a better country.
And the chapter's answer to them: "wherefore God is not ashamed to be called their God: for he hath prepared for them a city." A tent now; a city waiting. That's the packing list.

how: Christians read Hebrews 11 in worship and study, and some pray its opening line when facing a step whose end they can't see.

o: trusting God enough to step out before you can see
following rules strictly so that God rewards you
being completely sure how everything will end

s: faith in Hebrews 11 means believing without any reason
Hebrews calls it substance and evidence: solid ground for what isn't seen yet.
Abraham knew where he was going when he left
he went out, not knowing whither he went.
Hebrews says these all died not having received the promises
they saw them afar off, and greeted them anyway.

games.q: your older brother has a job offer in a city he's never seen. he says he can't decide until he knows exactly how it will turn out. what would by faith look like for him?
o: wait for a sign that guarantees it works out.
take the next step without seeing the end, packing light.
go, and cut every tie with home on the way out.
games.why: Abraham obeyed and went out, not knowing whither, and lived in tents: the next step taken, the end still unseen.

practice: Listen for one sound whose source you can't see: a car outside, a hum in the wall, a voice in another room. Stay with that one sound through the sit, real and close, though nothing in front of you shows where it comes from.

wordCard.voice: By faith. The two words Hebrews eleven keeps coming back to, name after name, starting with Abel.

orig.note: Greek: substance; the word behind substance in Hebrews 11:1.

carryVoice: One line for today: the evidence of things not seen, like Abraham packing for a place he'd never seen. See you tomorrow.
